ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation, screen all shareholders, directors, authorized signatories, beneficial owners, major counterparties and payment beneficiaries against United Nations Security Council lists, European Union financial-sanctions regulations, French national sanctions measures, OFAC sanctions lists where United States nexus or risk policy requires, and reputable commercial sanctions databases. Conduct PEP, family-member and close-associate screening under Code monétaire et financier Articles L561-10 and R561-18 to R561-20. Apply enhanced due diligence for PEPs, high-risk countries, opaque ownership chains, nominee arrangements, unexplained wealth, adverse media, public procurement exposure and high-risk payment intermediaries. France does not treat OFAC lists as universally binding absent a relevant United States nexus, but regulated institutions may apply them contractually or as risk controls. Retain screening evidence, source-of-wealth records, source-of-funds records and escalation decisions.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI), accessible through formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; trademark clearance is separately conducted through the INPI trademark database
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be stated in the incorporation documents and registry filing. French characters and Latin-script names are accepted. A foreign-language or transliterated name may be used provided it is not misleading, contrary to public policy, confusingly similar to an existing corporate name or trademark, or falsely suggestive of a regulated status. The SAS designation or an accepted equivalent must appear in the constitutional documents and prescribed corporate information. The registered name does not itself confer trademark protection. A French translation is generally required for foreign public documents submitted to French authorities.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque, bank, credit, crédit, finance, financier and comparable banking or financial-service terms without the required authorization
Assurance, insurance and comparable insurance terms without authorization
Mutuelle and other terms reserved for regulated mutual-insurance entities
Bourse, investment fund, société de gestion and comparable regulated-market or asset-management terms without authorization
Notaire, avocat, huissier, expert-comptable and other protected professional titles when use could imply unauthorized professional status
Université, école, institut and comparable education terms where use could imply an accredited educational institution
France, République française, national, ministère and comparable official or governmental references where use may imply public authority or official sponsorship
Terms implying a public-interest, charitable, diplomatic, military or intergovernmental status without legal basis
Names identical or confusingly similar to existing companies, trademarks, domain names or protected signs
Terms contrary to law, public order, morality or third-party rights
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not provide a general statutory company-name reservation mechanism with a uniform 30-day reservation period for SAS entities. Before filing, conduct INPI corporate-name, trademark, domain-name and trade-name searches and obtain a written name-availability opinion from French counsel or the filing agent. If the Guichet unique or registry rejects or suspends the filing, obtain the electronic rejection or deficiency notice, identify whether the issue concerns similarity, protected terminology, corporate-purpose wording, required supporting documents or identity verification, and submit corrected documents or a reasoned response through the prescribed INPI electronic workflow within the deadline stated in the notice. For a formal registry decision, use the available administrative or judicial challenge route identified in the decision, generally before the competent commercial court or administrative court depending on the challenged act. A rejected name may be amended in the constitutional documents and resubmitted; there is no automatic appeal that preserves priority over third-party use.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A French SAS must have a registered office in France under Code civil Article 1837 and Code de commerce provisions governing corporate registration. A commercial domiciliation provider may be used if it holds the required authorization and the parties execute a compliant domiciliation agreement under Code de commerce Articles L123-11-1 to L123-11-3 and R123-167 to R123-171. A home address may be used by the legal representative subject to statutory duration and landlord or lease restrictions. A purely virtual address without reliable document receipt, identity verification, customer access and operational records is unsuitable for banking, tax, AML or engineering-client due diligence. For offshore BIM, civil-infrastructure CAD and structural drafting, virtual domiciliation is legally possible at incorporation, but substantive operations should maintain accessible project records, qualified personnel or contractors, secure systems, client contracts, accounting records and evidence of actual management in France where French tax residence, transfer-pricing, professional-liability or public-procurement issues arise.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: No official national statistical rate is published. Indicative risk assessment for a newly incorporated, foreign-owned SAS using a domiciliation provider and conducting engineering CAD/BIM outsourcing is approximately 5% to 15% annually for an unannounced or short-notice physical verification by a competent authority, increasing materially where there is a VAT refund, payroll, public procurement, regulated-client relationship, inconsistent registered-office information, unexplained banking activity, suspected fictitious management or AML alert. This is a risk estimate, not a statutory probability. Maintain a functional registered office, appointment and access records, accounting and tax files, beneficial-owner evidence, employment or contractor records, cybersecurity controls and client/project documentation.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Code de commerce (French Commercial Code), Book II, Title II, Chapter VII — Arts. L. 227-1 to L. 227-27 (SAS regime); Arts. L. 227-2 and L. 225-13 (paid-up capital and common rules); Arts. R. 123-1, R. 123-101 et seq. (RCS registration); Décret n° 2021-300 (Guichet Unique e-filing procedures)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the judicial district of the registered office, operating through the INPI Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: M0 declaration (déclaration de création de personne morale) transmitted electronically with the executed statuts (Articles of Association) and all statutory attachments
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for an SAS; the articles fix the share capital freely, and a nominal capital of EUR 1,000 is recommended for this entity. Under Art. L. 225-13 applied through Art. L. 227-2, at least 50% of the nominal value of cash shares must be paid up at incorporation and deposited in a blocked escrow account (compte de consignation) at a French bank or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations; the funds are released only upon presentation of the K-bis registration extract.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST CORPORATE RESOLUTION OF THE SOLE SHAREHOLDER OF [COMPANY NAME] SAS — Adopted on [DATE] in [LOCATION]. RESOLVED: (1) that the Articles of Association of the company, presented to the sole shareholder, are hereby definitively adopted in their entirety; (2) that the subscribed share capital of EUR [AMOUNT], consisting of [NUMBER] ordinary shares of EUR [PAR VALUE] each, is acknowledged as fully subscribed, and the corresponding cash contributions have been deposited in a blocked account opened with [BANK], in accordance with Article L. 227-2 of the French Commercial Code; (3) that the registered office is fixed at [ADDRESS]; (4) that [FULL NAME] is appointed as Président, with full powers as legal representative; and (5) that the Président is authorized to complete all registration formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding shareholder(s) and, if real-property or in-kind contributions are made, a civil-law notaire and a commissaire aux apports
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the statuts under Code de commerce Arts. L. 227-1 et seq., specifying corporate name, duration (maximum 99 years), registered office, corporate object limited to BIM/CAD engineering services, share capital structure, governance rules, and the identity of the first Président. Each page and the signature page must be signed by all shareholders. If in-kind contributions are made, annex the commissaire aux apports valuation report. Complete the beneficial-owner declaration (DBE) and collate identity and address proof of all shareholders.
required_dossiers: Executed statuts (original signed paper or reliable electronic signature)
Valid passport or national ID of each shareholder and beneficial owner
Notarized power of attorney if a representative signs
Commissaire aux apports report (only for in-kind contributions)
Proof of registered-office occupancy (lease, free-of-charge loan, or ownership title)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the dossier is incomplete or refused by the guichet, correct the flagged fields and resubmit with a supplementary act; if notarization becomes necessary, execute a corrective instrument (acte rectificatif) before re-filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Blocked Deposit of Cash Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French credit institution or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked account in the name of the company 'en formation' and deposit at least 50% of the nominal value of the cash subscribed shares. The depository bank issues an attestation de dépôt des fonds, which is required for registration; the escrowed funds are released solely against the K-bis extract after RCS registration.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of the signatories and beneficial owners
Attestation de dépôt des fonds issued by the bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the selected bank declines the blocked account, transfer the deposit to another French bank or to the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations; if KYC documentation is challenged, furnish bank statements and source-of-funds affidavits.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the Formation Notice in a Legal Gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL) authorized in the département of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Place the avis de constitution containing the company name, legal form (SAS), share capital, registered office, corporate object, duration, and the identity of the Président. The gazette issues an attestation de parution that must be included in the registration file. Publication fees are negotiated directly with the JAL (typically EUR 120-250).
required_dossiers: Statutory particulars sheet for the editor (name, form, capital, object, duration, office, legal representative)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the avis omits a mandatory mention or contains an error, publish a corrective avis rectificatif in the same gazette and obtain a new attestation before filing with the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of the Incorporation Dossier with the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI — Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), which routes the file to the competent Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the M0 declaration online and upload the executed statuts, attestation de dépôt des fonds, attestation de parution, DBE, identity documents, and any powers of attorney. Pay the greffe taxes and levies directly on the portal. Monitor the processing dashboard and respond to any incompleteness queries within the statutory deadlines.
required_dossiers: Attestation de parution from the JAL
Identity documents of shareholders and beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a notice of incompleteness, cure the defects within 15 days through the portal; in case of outright refusal, contest the decision before the juge commis à la surveillance du registre of the tribunal de commerce.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS Registration and Issuance of K-bis Extract and Tax Identifiers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (via the INPI Guichet Unique pipeline)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the greffe validates the file, the company is inscribed in the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés and receives the SIREN/SIRET numbers, the official K-bis extract, and notification of its French VAT identification number. The K-bis is delivered electronically to the founder and presented to the escrow bank to release the consigned capital.
required_dossiers: Complete dossier transmitted by the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If issuance is delayed beyond the statutory period, lodge an expedited request with the greffe; erroneous mentions on the K-bis are corrected by filing a rectifying formalité on the Guichet Unique, with judicial recourse to the juge commis à la surveillance du registre if needed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Governance, Operating Bank Account, and Statutory Books
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Sole shareholder and Président of the SAS; commercial bank; INSEE/URSSAF automatic notifications
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ratify the statutes by formal decision, confirm the appointment of the Président (if not already fixed in the statutes), and authorize the opening of the operating bank account. Present the K-bis to the depository bank to release the unpaid 50% of capital into the operating account. Open the share register (registre des mouvements de titres), the decisions register (registre des décisions), and coordinate with the accountant for URSSAF, corporate tax (IS) filing cycles, and the CNIL (RGPD) data-processing register relevant to BIM service delivery.
required_dossiers: Written acceptance of office by the Président
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires updated corporate documents, use a certified registrar-issued K-bis; if the President's appointment is challenged, remedy by a new shareholder decision and, where applicable, register the appointment via a complementary M2-type filing on the Guichet Unique.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — the entity performs office-based digital CAD/BIM and structural drafting services and operates no industrial establishment subject to the ICPE (Installations Classées pour la Protection de l'Environnement) permitting regime. If the company later leases industrial premises, the competent authority would be the DREAL (Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — no operating or manufacturing permit is required under French law for engineering drafting services (ISIC 7110). Professional practice is unrestricted for BIM coordination, subject only to standard business registration (K-bis), employer declarations (URSSAF), and GDPR compliance (CNIL).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition Écologique et de la Cohésion des Territoires / DREAL — Service de l'Inspection des Installations Classées
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — the activity is a non-material digital service; no installation listed in the Environment Code annexes (Arts. L. 181-1, R. 122-2) is present, and no construction, discharge, or emissions thresholds are triggered.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater, VOC, or hazardous-waste streams arise from CAD/BIM drafting. Compliance with municipal non-domestic effluent rules (Code général des collectivités territoriales, Art. L. 1331-10) for sanitary office discharges and WEEE e-waste handling (Code de l'environnement, Arts. R. 543-178 et seq.) is required as a matter of ordinary office operation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety and evacuation certification of the office premises under Code du travail Arts. R. 4227-1 et seq., including ERP classification where the building is open to the public, structural load and electrical conformity attestations provided by the lessor under the bail commercial, annual workplace safety inspections, first-aid provisions, and emergency plans to be completed before personnel occupy the office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP), administered through the relevant Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE) and the Service des impôts des entreprises étrangères (SIEE) where applicable. Official portals: https://www.impots.gouv.fr and https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SAS is incorporated and registered through the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI). The registration filing generates the French SIREN and SIRET identifiers. The entity then registers for corporate income tax, VAT, payroll taxes, and other applicable taxes with the competent SIE through the business tax account on impots.gouv.fr. The French VAT identification number is issued by the DGFiP and generally consists of the prefix FR, a two-digit control key, and the nine-digit SIREN. A foreign entity without a French establishment must apply to the SIEE where French VAT registration is required; an EU-established business may in specified circumstances use the OSS or reverse-charge mechanisms instead of obtaining a French VAT number. Registration documentation generally includes constitutional documents, proof of registered office, directors' identification, business activity details, bank details, expected turnover, and evidence of the French taxable transactions.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SAS is generally subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS) by default. Eligible SAS entities may elect temporarily for partnership-style taxation under the French income tax regime (impôt sur le revenu, IR), generally for a maximum period of five fiscal years, subject to statutory conditions including size, age, ownership, activity, and shareholder requirements. The election is not an automatic check-the-box election and must be notified to the tax authority within the prescribed deadline. No general US-style entity-classification election exists. France applies anti-hybrid mismatch rules implementing the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive, which can deny deductions or impose income inclusion where applicable; these rules are not a taxpayer-selectable hybrid election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, VAT).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For the French VAT franchise regime applicable to services, the principal historical thresholds are EUR 37,500 of prior-year turnover and EUR 41,250 where the current-year turnover exceeds the preceding threshold. Thresholds are subject to statutory amendment and special rules. VAT registration may nevertheless be required without reliance on the domestic threshold, including for intra-Community acquisitions, imports, certain cross-border supplies, transactions subject to reverse charge, and taxable transactions connected with a French establishment. For B2B engineering, CAD, and BIM services supplied to a business customer established outside France, the place-of-supply and reverse-charge rules must be assessed separately; the transaction may not require French output VAT but may still require reporting or registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France does not currently operate a general real-time invoice-clearance system for all domestic transactions. Mandatory electronic invoicing for domestic B2B transactions established in France is being phased in through approved Partner Dematerialization Platforms (Plateformes de dématérialisation partenaires, PDPs): receipt capability for all businesses from 1 September 2026; issuance capability for large and mid-sized businesses from 1 September 2026; and issuance capability for small and micro-enterprises from 1 September 2027, subject to legally permitted adjustments. B2B invoices must contain mandatory VAT and transaction data and be transmitted through the prescribed platform architecture. Separate electronic reporting of transaction and payment data applies to transactions outside the domestic B2B e-invoicing scope, including certain exports, intra-Community transactions, and B2C transactions. There is no general French requirement for a digital tax stamp on each invoice.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from France to destinations outside the European Union may be exempt from French VAT with right to deduction if the supplier can demonstrate that the goods left the EU customs territory and that the statutory export conditions were satisfied. The supplier must retain the customs export declaration, Movement Reference Number (MRN), electronic exit confirmation or equivalent customs evidence, commercial invoice, transport documentation, and transaction records. Services require a separate analysis. B2B engineering, CAD, and BIM services are generally taxed according to the customer-location place-of-supply rule; services supplied to a business customer established outside France are generally outside the scope of French VAT, normally invoiced without French VAT with an appropriate place-of-supply and reverse-charge reference where applicable. This is not technically a French zero-rated export of goods. Services connected with French immovable property, including certain site-specific architectural or engineering services, may instead be taxable where the property is located.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic customs export declaration and Movement Reference Number (MRN)
Electronic customs exit result, exit certification, or other legally accepted proof that the goods exited the European Union
Commercial invoice identifying the exporter, consignee, goods, value, and contractual terms
Bill of lading, air waybill, CMR consignment note, or other transport evidence, as applicable
Packing list and export-related transport or logistics records
Customer purchase order, contract, and delivery evidence
Proof of payment and accounting records linking the payment to the export transaction
Customer VAT identification and reverse-charge evidence for cross-border B2B services, where applicable

Inward remittance certificate only where specifically required by a financing, banking, or foreign-jurisdiction procedure; France does not generally require an inward remittance certificate as a condition for VAT export exemption
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France does not impose a general statutory 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export proceeds. Unsupported or incorrectly applied VAT exemption may be reassessed as French VAT, together with late-payment interest generally calculated at the statutory monthly rate and tax penalties. A 40% penalty may apply for deliberate failure or deliberate inaccuracy, and an 80% penalty may apply for fraudulent manoeuvres or abuse of rights, subject to statutory conditions. Incorrect customs declarations may trigger customs duties, import VAT reassessment, customs penalties, seizure, or loss of customs simplifications. Serious VAT fraud may also create criminal exposure. Export documentation must be retained for the applicable French accounting and tax limitation period, generally at least six years for tax records, with longer retention potentially required under commercial, customs, or accounting rules.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), acting under the regulatory and supervisory framework of the French Treasury (Direction Générale du Trésor) and the Prudential Supervision and Resolution Authority (ACPR - Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France applies full current-account and capital-account convertibility under EU law (Article 63 TFEU). Current-account payments for services, fees and royalties are freely transferable without prior exchange-control authorisation. Capital-account operations, including foreign direct investment, portfolio investment and intercompany loans, are also liberalised, subject only to (i) prior authorisation for direct investments in sensitive/strategic sectors (e.g. defence, artificial intelligence, critical infrastructure) under the French FDI screening framework and (ii) mandatory beneficial-ownership and anti-money-laundering declarations. Profit remittance is unrestricted in foreign-exchange terms, but attracts a domestic dividend withholding tax of 25% unless reduced by an applicable double-tax treaty or eliminated by the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for qualifying EU parent companies. No exchange-control licensing is required for converting EUR into foreign currency or repatriating profits, provided the transfer is executed through an ACPR-authorised credit institution and is declared for balance-of-payments statistical purposes, typically on a currency-by-currency basis in stable economic monetary policy conditions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France does not impose a mandatory surrender or fixed mandatory conversion ratio of export proceeds into EUR. Exporters may lawfully retain foreign-currency receipts in a foreign-currency account opened with a French credit institution. The statutory repatriation/collection timeline for trade and services receivables from non-residents is governed by the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier) and commercial payment rules, generally requiring that export receivables be collected and made available in France within 180 days from the due date or from service completion, unless the exporter's credit institution grants a contractual extension. The mandatory conversion ratio is therefore 0% (no statutory obligation to convert export receipts into euros). All cross-border payments in excess of EUR 10,000 per calendar month or per transaction must be reported to Banque de France in the framework of the balance-of-payments (BOP) statistical declaration, regardless of the currency nominated.

Operational Multi-Currency Account and Capital Contribution Escrow Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole CIB (Corporate and Investment Banking)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High for EU/EEA-licensed Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) passported into France under PSD2, such as Qonto, Wise, N26 or Revolut, for operational payment flows and low-value disbursements. Low for offshore digital EMIs domiciled outside the EU/EEA. Legal constraints: an offshore (non-EU/EEA) EMI without a French ACPR licence or EU passport cannot provide a French-issued IBAN, cannot act as a formal custodian of French registered capital, cannot issue the statutory certificate of deposit (certificat de dépositaire de fonds) required during incorporation of a SAS, and is not accepted by French tax or treasury authorities for balance-of-payments reporting. Even EU-licensed EMIs are not admitted for capital escrow accounts or as the primary treasury bank for large-value cross-border settlements; a fully licensed French credit institution or a French branch of a European credit institution remains mandatory for statutory corporate treasury functions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A face-to-face KYC interview is mandatory for the legal representative (Président) of the French SAS, at least during the first account opening, before the account is activated for cross-border transactions. For non-resident directors or beneficial owners, physical presence at a branch of the tier-1 bank is generally required. Remote account opening is available only in narrowly defined cases: (i) the legal representative must be an EU/EEA resident holding a valid eIDAS-qualified electronic signature; (ii) the beneficial owners must be identifiable through a trusted European AML/KYC database; and (iii) the company must have a physical registered office in France verifiable by bank diligence. Where the beneficial owner is a non-EEA corporate entity or individual, remote opening is normally rejected, and a physical meeting of both the director and the ultimate beneficial owner (or a documented legal proxy) is imposed by ACPR guidance on politically exposed persons and effective beneficial-ownership verification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated SAS with negligible paid-in capital and no operational history, opening a multi-currency account without clear source of funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: K-bis extract (certificate of registration), notarised articles of association (statuts), certificate of capital deposit (certificat de dépositaire de fonds), signed board/shareholder resolutions approving initial funding, business plan with cash-flow projections, letters of intent from target clients, proof of registered office lease, and source-of-funds declaration for all initial capital payments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident corporate director or shareholder creating an opaque beneficial-ownership layer for a French SAS engaged in cross-border BIM/CAD outsourcing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Beneficial-ownership declaration filed with the French Trade Register (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs), notarised and apostilled passport copies of all natural-person directors and beneficial owners, proof of tax residence (tax residence certificates), organisational chart showing ultimate ownership >25%, ratified board resolutions appointing the French resident representative, and bank references from the shareholder's existing banking relationships.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border invoice flows from foreign clients in engineering and drafting services, triggering bank concerns over transfer pricing, trade-based money laundering, or tax evasion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Industry-accepted commercial contracts (master service agreements, statements of work), invoices with coherent ISIC 7110 / NAICS 541330 classification, transfer-pricing documentation under French TP rules, FATCA/CRS statements, evidence of VAT registration or applicable VAT exemption, detailed service descriptions proving genuine engineering/CAD activity, and audited projections of transaction volumes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sudden high-velocity receipts from a concentrated client base or transactions routed through third-party jurisdictions, regarded as a treasury red flag for kun-recycling or illicit structuring.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Cash-flow forecast and annual treasury projection, client onboarding files with KYC on foreign counterparties, underlying commercial agreements, payment schedule and invoice ageing report, SWIFT or SEPA payment evidence, shareholder declarations confirming business purpose, and a sworn statement by the French director explaining the commercial substance of each payment stream.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections must be completed by bank wire transfer using ISO 20022 SEPA Credit Transfer (pain.001) for EUR payments or SWIFT MT103 for non-EUR currencies. The receiving bank must be an ACPR-authorised credit institution in France holding the capital contribution either on a blocked account in the name of the SAS in formation or on a dedicated capital escrow account. The exact payment purpose code must be indicated: use Banque de France/European BOP purpose group 'CAPA' (capital payments) or 'INVE' for direct investment equity contributions; where the shareholder is a foreign direct investor, the bank will map the instruction to the French BOP item 'Direct Investment - Equity Capital'. Field 70 must explicitly contain 'APPORT CAPITAL SOCIAL' and a reference to the acte de constitution. Verification: the depositary bank issues a non-negotiable certificate of deposit ('certificat de dépôt des fonds') listing the subscribed capital amount, the account holder, and the release conditions upon registration of the SAS; release of funds to the permanent operating account is permitted only after production of the K-bis extract and the registrar's approval decision.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for trade settlements and subcontractor payments should follow the following clearing rails: EUR payments inside the European Union must be executed via SEPA Credit Transfer (pain.001) in TARGET2 for large-value RTGS payments; non-EUR payments must be dispatched via SWIFT MT103 with strict field discipline, including correct beneficiary bank BIC, correspondent routing, and mandatory purpose code. For engineering/CAD services, pure service disbursements are settled by bank transfer; commercial letters of credit (UCP 600) are appropriate only where the invoice bundles hardware deliverables, certified infrastructure equipment or a construction phase requiring documentary evidence of dispatch. All outbound payments must be supported by the underlying commercial invoice, contract, and, where applicable, a summary of services rendered; payments exceeding EUR 10,000 per month or per transaction trigger Banque de France balance-of-payments declaration. If an escrow arrangement is required for large infrastructure contracts, the escrow account must be maintained at a licensed French or EU credit institution and governed by a French-law escrow agreement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain vanilla FX forward (change à terme) executed with a licensed French or EU credit institution, documented as a non-speculative hedge under French accounting principles
FX swap (swap de change) for short-term liquidity and rolling settlement of cross-currency obligations, subject to EMIR clearing/reporting thresholds
Cross-currency interest rate swap (CCIRS) used for hedging multi-year infrastructure contracts or project finance debt denominated in foreign currency

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) with cash settlement, used only when the underlying currency is not deliverable in the French market due to settlement restrictions; must be executed with a regulated bank, subject to the same hedge documentation obligations as deliverable forwards

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate tax return (Déclaration de résultats – liasse fiscale forms 2065/2065-SD)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 December fiscal year-end: the second business day following 3 May (typically 5 May). For a non-calendar year-end: within 3 months of the fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 10% of the net tax due, increasing to 40% after a 30-day formal notice; monthly late-payment interest at 0.2%. Persistent non-filing allows DGFiP default assessment, tax liens, and enforcement against assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing (dépôt des comptes annuels with RCS registration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registry of the Commercial Court)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of fiscal year-end; for a 31 December year-end, by 31 July. Extension can be requested by court order before the deadline.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: After formal notice, court-ordered injunction to file under a daily penalty (astreinte); fines up to EUR 1,500 for the company and EUR 5,000 for its president; repeated omission or failure to regularise can trigger administrative radiation (strike-off) from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership register update / confirmation (Déclaration des Bénéficiaires Effectifs – DBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (as part of the RCS file)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of any change in beneficial ownership; no yearly re-filing is required if there have been no changes. The RCS data is validated when annual accounts are filed.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to update DBE exposes a fine of up to EUR 10,000 for individuals and EUR 20,000 for legal persons; false declaration is punishable by imprisonment up to 6 months and EUR 7,500 fine. The public prosecutor may seek dissolution for repeated non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CET annual declarations – CFE and CVAE (local economic contribution)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: CFE is payable by 15 December of the tax year according to the annual tax notice; no separate annual declaration is required for a continuing establishment. CVAE annual declaration (form 1330-CVAE) is filed with the corporate tax return by the 3 May + 2 business days deadline for calendar-year companies.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 10% of the CET amount, increased to 40% after formal notice; monthly 0.2% interest; recovery by enforcement notice (avis de mise en recouvrement) and tax lien on business property.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A French SAS must appoint a statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) when, at fiscal year-end, it exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds: total balance sheet assets over EUR 4,000,000; net annual turnover over EUR 8,000,000; more than 50 employees. Exceptions apply if the company belongs to a consolidated group, is a holding company, or voluntarily appoints an auditor.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Individual statutory accounts must be prepared under French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général – PCG). IFRS as endorsed by the EU is permitted for consolidated accounts of listed companies and, under certain conditions, for non-listed companies; it is not permitted for the individual annual accounts of an SAS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: UBO declarations (DBE) are maintained on a continuous basis and updated only upon a shareholding or control change; filing is mandatory within 30 days of such change. There is no separate annual UBO confirmation filing. The registry verifies DBE accuracy when the annual accounts are deposited.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (registre des titres or registre des mouvements de titres)
Register of Directors and Officers (registre des décisions et délibérations)
Minute Book (procès-verbaux des assemblées et des décisions)
